findings.location: allowlists.json kinds.Pod.RULED_OUT_BY_MANIFEST 'imagePullPolicy (AlwaysPullImages)': 'MC33'; scripts/admission_semantics_v2.py check_manifest (MC33 checks containers and initContainers only), final_object (AlwaysPullImages block), _validations A2-POD-PULL-POLICY; upstream plugin/pkg/admission/alwayspullimages/admission.go:76-81 (sha256 325c6870...)
findings.finding:
AlwaysPullImages is in the W02g allowlist, and at v1.37.1 its Admit also rewrites every image volume: 'for _, v := range pod.Spec.Volumes { if v.Image != nil { v.Image.PullPolicy = api.PullAlways } }' (KEP-4639). No manifest constraint touches image volumes. MC33 covers only containers and initContainers, and MC36 only checks the volume name. No A2 validation reads spec.volumes[*].image: the echo carries volume names only, and A2-POD-PULL-POLICY reads containers and initContainers only. With AlwaysPullImages enabled, a signed Pod with an image volume whose pullPolicy is IfNotPresent (set explicitly, or defaulted for a digest reference) is persisted with pullPolicy Always, and A2 admits it.
- Probe PA: check_manifest returns None for the positive Pod plus volume {name: data, image: {reference: <digest>, pullPolicy: IfNotPresent}} with the echo 'data'.
- final_object with alwaysPullImages true leaves the volume unchanged, so the model omits the upstream mutation.
- check_final on the object with the upstream mutation applied returns None.
The allowlist's own defaulting row says 'it is forced to Always for every container and image volume', yet the disposition table cites only MC33. This violates rule 1 of A2 (every field an enabled mutator can set is allowed, server-chosen, or ruled out by a constraint that A2 re-checks). The effect is benign, since it forces a stricter pull. The completeness claim is still false.
findings.requiredChange:
Do one of the following:
- extend MC33 to image volumes (pullPolicy Always, reference pinned by digest) and add an A2 check such as '!has(object.spec.volumes) || object.spec.volumes.all(v, !has(v.image) || v.image.pullPolicy == "Always")';
- forbid image volumes in qualification manifests (new MC code) and in A2.
Add the AlwaysPullImages volume mutation to final_object and the allowlist dispositions. Add a manifest vector, an end-to-end vector with alwaysPullImages and an image volume, and a finalObject vector.

findings.location: admission-manifests/planeon-a2.json planeon-a2-configmap.static.k8s.io (matches every CONFIGMAP CREATE in the namespace; A2-RESERVED, A2-CM-IMMUTABLE); README 'The sealed directory'; W01 HOST_INTERFACE_SPEC.md §2.5 row 'Root-CA ConfigMap publisher | Keeps one ConfigMap per namespace | Counted in observed usage'; upstream pkg/controller/certificates/rootcacertpublisher/publisher.go:41-46, 196-212
findings.finding:
The per-kind A2 policies match every CREATE of their kind in the qualification namespace, whoever creates it. Their validations assume a signed manifest: no reserved keys, immutable, shape echo. kube-controller-manager's root-CA publisher creates 'kube-root-ca.crt' in every namespace. That ConfigMap carries the annotation 'kubernetes.io/description' and is not immutable.
- Probe PB: check_final on the publisher's object returns A2-RESERVED.
- Without the annotation it returns A2-CM-IMMUTABLE.
Whenever the qualification namespace is created, or the ConfigMap is deleted, while the static directory is loaded, the publisher's CREATE is denied forever. The controller then retries with rate limiting. This contradicts the W01 §2.5 disposition, which treats the ConfigMap as an expected object counted in observed usage. The README and the allowlist do not mention non-gate creators. An implementer copying the policies would break an upstream controller in that namespace. Qualification Pods do not need the ConfigMap, because automount is false and kube-api-access volumes are forbidden, so this is a liveness and contract conflict, not a safety hole. UPDATE is not matched, so a ConfigMap that already exists is unaffected.
findings.requiredChange:
Decide and state how non-gate creators in the qualification namespace are handled. Options:
- admit exactly the publisher's object, identified by name kube-root-ca.crt and the root-ca-cert-publisher controller identity (request.userInfo.username), and keep A2 for every other creator;
- require that the namespace and its kube-root-ca.crt pre-exist before the directory is sealed, and amend W01 §2.5's disposition, noting that a recreation is denied.
Add vectors (publisher object admitted or explicitly refused) and record the decision in the README and allowlists.json.

findings.location: README POLICY-ADMISSION-SEMANTICS/v2 A2 item 1 ('ruled out by a manifest constraint, which A2 re-checks on the final object'), 'Manifest constraints' section; allowlists.json RULED_OUT_BY_MANIFEST ('requests copied from limits': MC34, 'LimitRanger defaults and annotation': MC34, 'fields of disabled feature gates': 'manifest content (W03 signer)'); scripts/admission_semantics_v2.py check_claim (A2 branch)
findings.finding:
Several dispositions rely on a manifest constraint that A2 does not and cannot re-check.
- MC34: A2 has no resources check.
- MC33's digest pin.
- MC35, MC36.
- Disabled-gate fields, which have no MC code at all, and which DropDisabledPodFields removes before A2 can see them.
Probes:
- PC: a limits-only manifest fails MC34, yet final_object copies the requests and check_final returns None.
- PC2: a tag image with Always fails MC33, and check_final returns None.
- PD: check_claim accepts an A2 claim with only the hash, plugin and A1 evidence. Nothing ties A1's signed bytes to check_manifest.
The soundness argument therefore depends on the W03 signer enforcing check_manifest. The text says A2 re-checks it, which overstates A2.
findings.requiredChange: Reword A2 item 1: each disposition is either re-checked by A2 or guaranteed by the signed manifest, and say which constraint is which. List the disabled-gate rule as a signer obligation with the gate set pinned by W02g SC15, or give it an MC code. Add an evidence key, for example manifestConstraintsMetAtSigning, to the A2 claim in check_claim, or state that a1AdmittedSignedBytes implies check_manifest at enrollment. Add the corresponding claim vector.

findings.location: README 'The sealed directory' ('Static policies also run for these requests; API-registered ones never do'); upstream staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/policy/generic/plugin.go:58-65, 309-330

findings.location: README 'The directory is reloaded at most every minute when its contents change'; upstream staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/filesystem/watchuntil.go (fsnotify events call the handler immediately; the ticker polls every interval); policy/manifest/source/source.go:33, 139-170
findings.finding: Reload is event-driven (fsnotify) and also polled every minute. A change is picked up immediately, and within a minute at the latest. It is not limited to 'at most every minute'. On a load or compile failure the old hooks stay and last_config_info keeps the old hash. That is correct for the observer and worth stating.
findings.requiredChange: Reword: reloaded on a filesystem event and at least every minute. A failed load keeps the previous configuration and its hash.

questionAnswers.Q1:
Mostly faithful.
- A2 placement is amended as the owner decided: a static, run-independent sealed directory, not I07. The pin by admissionPolicy and mutationBroker digests becomes the loaded manifest hash.
- A3 and A4 match W01 §3.2. A3 uses the I05 v2 drain answer, with PENDING meaning wait and HELD meaning no write.
- The guarantee and the non-claims match §3.2 and §3.3.
- The v1 sentence is quoted exactly: POLICY_OBSERVATION_READINESS.md lines 139-141, digest verified. check_claim refuses it (C01, vectors Q01 onward).
Gaps:
- F4: the A1 text drops 'scope' and 'observed policy generation', which C11 still requires; there is also the 'four checks' wording.
- F3: check_claim accepts A2 without evidence that the manifest met the constraints, while the text says A2 re-checks them.
questionAnswers.Q2:
Mostly complete. I verified each mutating plugin's Admit at the pinned commit:
- ServiceAccount: default SA name and alias, token volume and mounts only with effective automount, pull secrets copied only when none are listed; mirror-pod path ruled out by MC04.
- DefaultTolerationSeconds: the two tolerations, appended unless a matching key or effect exists.
- Priority: priority 0 and PreemptLowerPriority only with no globalDefault; otherwise priorityClassName is set.
- LimitRanger: defaults only for missing keys, and always the kubernetes.io/limit-ranger annotation.
- RuntimeClass: only with runtimeClassName.
- PodTopologyLabels: only with nodeName.
The validation-only plugins and the create-path ordering, BeforeCreate and Service allocation rows agree with the cited code. All 95 cited files match their digests.
Gap (F1): AlwaysPullImages also forces spec.volumes[*].image.pullPolicy, which no MC rules out and A2 does not check.
Side note on W02g: its ALLOWED_ADMISSION comment calls AlwaysPullImages one of the plugins that 'only restrict requests'. It mutates, which this contract correctly treats it as doing.
questionAnswers.Q3:
With the closed mutator set (SC05, OR06, the static guard) and A1's byte check, I found one way for a delta outside the allowlist to persist while every A2 validation passes: F1, AlwaysPullImages on image volumes.
Cluster-state levers checked:
- ServiceAccount pull secrets or automount: E05, E12.
- A globalDefault PriorityClass: E06, and a lowest-value default still sets priorityClassName.
- LimitRange defaults: the annotation is always set, so A2-RESERVED.
- Toleration flags: E09.
- RuntimeClass and Node labels: gated by forbidden fields.
- ServiceCIDR and family: E10, E11.
Each is refused or harmless.
The shape echo argument is sound within its stated bound: a mutator that rewrote both a field and its echo would have to be outside W02g and OR06.
Dependency (F3): the argument relies on the signer enforcing check_manifest. MC34, MC33's digest pin, MC35, MC36 and disabled-gate fields are not re-checked by A2.
Controller side effects after CREATE (pods/binding labels, nodeName) are outside A2, as W01 §3.3 states.
questionAnswers.Q4:
The expressions are valid as far as static reading of v1.37.1 shows. I compiled nothing.
- Compile environment: object is DynType (cel/compile.go:254).
- Libraries (environment/base.go): ext.Strings v2 'join' over a traits.Lister of strings (cel-go ext/strings.go:539-552), the Regex 'matches' with a valid RE2 literal, the CIDR 'containsIP(string)' overload (library/cidr.go:128-129), and the standard macros exists_one, all and map.
- Runtime view: SchemalessTypedToVal (cel/common/valuesschemalesstyped.go). has() and map membership follow omitempty, so empty labels and annotations maps, imagePullSecrets, initContainers and an empty toleration value are absent. Pointer fields (priority, automount, immutable, tolerationSeconds) are present when set, and ints come through as int, so the comparisons are int==int.
- The types.go:330-331 doc comment about root metadata is not enforced on this path: labels and annotations are reachable.
- Static policies with a compile error fail the load (validating/plugin.go:85-90). A runtime error under failurePolicy Fail denies, so failures are closed.
check_final matches the CEL on reachable inputs. F7 lists divergences that only unreachable inputs trigger.
Guard:
- It matches the six resources at all versions. resourceRules without '/status' do not match the status subresource (webhook/predicates/rules/rules.go resource()), so the W02g validatingadmissionpolicy-status-controller (STATUS_ONLY) is not blocked.
- Static hooks run for the four policy resources even though API hooks are exempt (generic/plugin.go:315-327).
- Nothing the cluster needs writes these objects.
A per-kind policy does block a required controller: F2, kube-root-ca.crt.
questionAnswers.Q5:
Correct.
- Loader rules: names end in .static.k8s.io and are unique per kind; paramKind and paramRef are refused; binding policyName must carry the suffix and reference a policy in the directory (policy/manifest/loader/loader.go, manifest/validation.go).
- The kube-apiserver loader registers metav1.List as unversioned v1 List and decodes strictly (pkg/admission/plugin/policy/manifest/loader/validating_loader.go), so the one-file v1 List loads.
- manifest_directory_hash matches manifest/loader.go LoadFiles: os.ReadDir name order, directories skipped, lower-cased .yaml, .yml or .json extension, empty files skipped, each file's content followed by a NUL, 'sha256:%x', and '' when nothing has data.
- The committed file equals manifest_file_bytes, and its hash equals pinned.manifestDirectoryHash (cfb24e4e...).
- The metric is apiserver_manifest_admission_config_controller_last_config_info{plugin, apiserver_id_hash, hash}, ALPHA (manifest/metrics/metrics.go).
- check_a2_objects S01-S06 are stricter than the loader, which is fine. Loader defaulting adds empty selectors after load, which does not affect the pin.
questionAnswers.Q7: No overclaim found. The README and model say DATA_CHECK_ONLY: nothing contacts an apiserver, compiles CEL, installs an admission configuration or selects a distribution. W02c-F (I07 writes no admission objects), the sealed values, staticManifestsDir, the observer hash check and the signer are listed as open, and all E01-E12 stay OPEN_UNPROVEN. The one overstatement is F3: A2 're-checks' constraints that only the signer can guarantee.
